verification.notes: Finding classification is correct: Section 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but 7(a)-(c) contain only liability caps, a damages allocation and an attorneys'-fee waiver, and the only IP hook is the bare non-infringement warranty in 5(c). No Contractor IP indemnity existed, which is walk-away territory, so a redline is warranted. All seven fallback elements are met in operative language: IP indemnity, the three customary exclusions, the procure/modify/replace remedy ladder, a refund fallback, and a 3x annual fees super-cap. Preferred level is not reached: the insertion has no express duty to defend, no affiliate coverage, no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct triggers, and no notice/control/cooperation procedure. The Customer-indemnity element passes only because no Company-side indemnity exists to narrow. Minimality holds: the only collateral edit is the narrow conforming carve-out in 7(a) ("PARAGRAPH 7(d) OR"), which is necessary for the super-cap element to have effect; the drafter added no survival tail, no attorneys'-fee or damages language, no claims procedure and no Company-side indemnity, and retained 7(a)'s Company-favourable cap on Company's own liability, 7(c) and the 5(c) warranty unchanged. Intent is preserved: the third-party indemnity does not conflict with 7(c)'s waiver of attorneys' fees in suits between the parties, and the pre-existing Paragraph 9 carve-out in 7(a) survives. Drafting fix (not an element failure): the inserted paragraph is rendered without a "(d)" designator while both the amended 7(a) and the paragraph itself refer to "Paragraph 7(d)". Label the insertion "(d)" expressly so the cross-reference is not dangling. Optional escalation if the counterparty engages: add "defend" and "and its affiliates" plus a short notice/control/cooperation mechanic to move from fallback toward the preferred position.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The ownership bargain sits at or above our fallback and no redline is warranted. Section 4(a) vests all SOW work product (the "Works", expressly including data, computer programs and documentation) in Clear Capital, conditioned only on the work having been invoiced and paid — consistent with our position that we own what we pay for — and §6(b)/§7(c) add an express "hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress". Section 4(b) leaves RadialSpark with its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies and know-how, which is acceptable, and §4(c) gives us a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use, copy and modify any Contractor's Information embedded in the Works for our business operations, reinforced by §4(d) (we may make changes ourselves or through third parties without further payment). No Clear Capital IP or data is assigned or licensed to RadialSpark: §5(b) carves out "rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company", and §8 bars Contractor from using or disclosing our Confidential Information (expressly including Company records and data) without our express prior written permission, so there is no standing Vendor data licence to narrow. There is no joint ownership in the document. Short of preferred only in minor respects we note but do not flag: the §4(c) licence is not labelled "irrevocable" or "worldwide", and there is no standalone sentence declaring that we retain all rights in Clear Capital data.

quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services")
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binds Clear Capital anywhere in the Agreement. The engagement is expressly task-by-task through individually agreed Statements of Work (§ 1(a)), with no requirements commitment, minimum volume, or prohibition on procuring comparable services from third parties; § 3 compensation is purely time-and-materials per SOW and is not tied to exclusive engagement. The only uses of "exclusive" are Contractor's ownership of its pre-existing materials (§ 4, p0020), a non-exclusive licence in our favour (p0021), and the entire-agreement clause (p0051) — none of which restrict our sourcing freedom. The sole restrictive covenant is a mutual non-solicitation of employees (p0047), which is not exclusivity. This meets the preferred position; no redline needed.

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: The agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, stipulated-damages, minimum-fee or early-termination-fee construct payable by Clear Capital. Termination is available to either party for any or no reason on 15 days' notice (§ 6(a)) and on uncured material breach (§ 6(b)), and the only payment consequence in §§ 6(b) and 7(c) is Contractor's actual fees and expenses "incurred or earned … through the effective date of such termination" — compensation for work actually performed, not a liquidated amount. Compensation (§ 3) is time-and-materials with no late-payment penalty, non-refundable minimum, or termination charge; the non-solicitation clause (§ 13) carries no placement or buy-out fee; and § 7 caps liability by reference to fees paid rather than stipulating damages. This meets the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties, so no redline is proposed. Noted only for completeness: § 5's anti-bribery clause and the liability caps operate in our favour or neutrally and are not liquidated-damages exposure.

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language by a single appended sentence to Section 4(c) (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor without Contractor approval). The claimed deviation status and fallback target are correct, since the original Section 4(c) ran only to Clear Capital and Section 10 barred transfer without consent. Preferred level is incomplete for two reasons the drafter would need to repair if pursuing it: (i) no express extension to "contractors acting on Company's behalf" in the grant, and (ii) no express "irrevocable" qualifier on the perpetual paid-up grant. The successor-transfer wording is also limited to merger/acquisition successors rather than successors generally. Minimal: the edit is one concise insertion, adds no survival tail, expense, procedure, or notice-period boilerplate, and does not touch the favourable existing perpetual/royalty-free/sublicensable grant or delete any word (including the Customer-favourable "non-exclusive" and consent-not-unreasonably-withheld language in Section 10). No duplicate affiliate coverage arises because "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone with no affiliate inclusion. Preserves intent: Section 10's general non-assignment of the Agreement survives and continues to govern assignment of the Agreement and obligations; the inserted sentence is a specific, self-executing permission limited to the Section 4(c) licence, avoiding a broad "notwithstanding" override, and leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference (Section 4(c) is cited accurately). Drafting nit only (not a defect): "affiliates" is used without a defined term in the Agreement; if the counterparty pushes back, add a short definition of Affiliate (control-based) rather than expanding the operative grant.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The agreement contains no non-compete, exclusivity, territory or field-of-use covenant binding Company: § 1 (purpose/scope), § 4 (ownership), § 6 (termination) and § 7 (general terms) impose no limit on the businesses Company may operate or the products it may buy, build or license, and searches for "compete/competitor", "exclusive/exclusivity/restriction" and "shall not" return nothing of that character. The two use-limiting provisions are out of scope for this rule: (i) p0020 ("Company shall not resell or make use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives under this Agreement") is licence scope over Contractor's own pre-existing materials and records, not a restriction on Company's own products, brand or business — and p0021 in fact grants Company a perpetual, sublicensable licence over Contractor's Information incorporated into the Works for Company's business operations; and (ii) p0047 is a mutual one-year employee non-solicit, an employment covenant that binds Vendor equally and is not a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business. The preferred position ("Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction") is therefore satisfied on the document as drafted, so no redline is proposed.

quote: 10. NONASSIGNABILITY. Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: Section 10 is the only assignment provision; there is no change-of-control trigger anywhere (Section 6 termination rights are mutual for convenience and breach, not change of control), so no Vendor exit right needs deletion. The clause is mutual and applies a reasonableness standard to consent, but it subjects every assignment, including an assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, to the Contractor's prior consent. That fails the fallback requirement of a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, so we have added that carve-out only, leaving the existing consent and reasonableness mechanics (which already satisfy the remaining fallback elements) untouched.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the inserted lead-in creates a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice, and the pre-existing consent plus not-unreasonably-withheld mechanics survive verbatim to cover the remaining two elements. Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Company, no competitor bar on Contractor assignment, and the successor carve-out is mutual so Contractor can also assign without Company's consent. If the drafter wants preferred, the edit must be one-directional ("Except for an assignment by Company to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, upon written notice...") and add "and in no event to a competitor of Company". The change-of-control element is satisfied vacuously — the agreement contains no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger and no Vendor termination right keyed to one, so nothing needs deleting. Minimality holds: a single inserted exception clause; the existing mutual prohibition, the subcontracting reference, the express prior written consent requirement and the reasonableness standard are all retained unchanged, with no survival tails, notice procedures, or other extras. Intent is preserved: no defined term is disturbed, no cross-reference is left dangling, and the retained sentence is internally consistent with the new exception (the exception is drafted as a carve-out from, not a contradiction of, the consent requirement). Note only that "successor" is left undefined; if counterparty resists, tightening it to "successor in interest by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" would remove ambiguity without changing the position. The "deviation" classification is supportable: as originally drafted every assignment, including a corporate-transaction successor assignment, was gated on the other party's consent, which fails the fallback's mutual successor-on-notice element.

quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced, including, to the extent applicable to a particular engagement, the dates of Services and hours worked at the applicable rate by Statement of Work.
rationale: The agreement grants RadialSpark no audit, inspection, verification or usage-review right against Clear Capital. Compensation is time-and-materials, verified through Contractor's own invoices and supporting detail (§ 3(b)), and the only access provisions run the other way — Contractor's personnel must comply with Company's security and system-access policies when at a Company facility (§ 1(c)). Searches for audit, inspection, records, verification, compliance monitoring and system access return nothing, and §§ 1, 3 and 4 contain no such right. Because there is no Vendor audit right to constrain, the AUDIT rule's frequency, notice, off-site, auditor-independence, cost-allocation and no-system-access limits are unnecessary; the absence of any audit right is more protective than either the preferred or fallback position. We therefore do not propose inserting audit machinery against ourselves.

verification.notes: Position-complete at the preferred level: both preferred elements are met in operative language (New York governing law in Section 11; exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over the merits in Section 19 with a carve-out confined to temporary injunctive relief). The original clause was a genuine deviation and walk-away risk: Arizona law (outside the accepted set) plus mandatory binding arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules with no court venue provision, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note. Minimality holds. In Section 11 only the two jurisdiction words changed, with the severability sentence and the conflict-of-laws tail intact. In Section 19 the excised text (the binding-arbitration referral, the arbitration rules citation, and the award-confirmation sentence keyed to the arbitrator) is exactly what had to go to install a court forum; the heading change from "Arbitration" to "Jurisdiction" is required to avoid a retained heading contradicting the operative text. No survival tails, fee-shifting, jury-waiver, service-of-process, or other boilerplate extras were added. Intent is preserved: the defined term "Disputes" and its broad scope (common law, statutory, equitable; before or after the Effective Date; clauses (b) and (c) covering other agreements and dealings) are retained unchanged, and the "Except as otherwise specified below" lead-in now points to the retained temporary-injunctive-relief proviso rather than to a deleted arbitration exception, so no dangling cross-reference or undefined term results. No action required from the drafter; the fallback is correctly offered in the margin comment as an alternative rather than being relied on in the operative text.

quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.

New work only arises by mutually executed Statements of Work (p0004: "Statements of Work that are from time to time agreed upon shall reference this Agreement, and shall be executed by the parties"), so continued engagement effectively requires mutual written agreement rather than an automatic renewal. Because renewal is not automatic, the conditional automatic-renewal elements (12-month renewal term, 60-day Vendor reminder) and the renewal price-uplift cap are not engaged, and there is no non-renewal notice window to shorten. Noted but not flagged here: Section 3(b) (p0014) gives Contractor a unilateral right to change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap; that is a mid-term pricing mechanic rather than a renewal uplift and belongs to the pricing rule, not RENEWAL. No redline proposed under this rule.

Preferred is not complete for four reasons the drafter would have to repair if aiming higher: (i) the CGL limit is not expressed as "per occurrence"; (ii) no USD 2,000,000 aggregate limit is stated; (iii) E&O remains at USD 1,000,000 rather than USD 2,000,000; and (iv) cyber cover is USD 2,000,000 rather than the USD 5,000,000 required where Customer Data is processed. Workers' compensation and certificates-on-request are already met. Minimality holds: the edit is one added sentence confined to the single unmet fallback element. It adds no at-own-expense wording, no one-year survival tail, no notice or additional-insured procedures, and deletes nothing from the favourable retained text (workers' comp, CGL, E&O, certificates, material-change notice all survive intact). Intent is preserved: the new sentence sits alongside, and does not contradict, the existing coverage list; the existing certificates provision refers to "the above coverage" and now naturally captures the new line without any dangling term or cross-reference. Optional tightening only (not a defect for scoring): the inserted sentence relies on "also" to inherit the opening "Throughout the term of this Agreement" duration. If you want the temporal anchor beyond argument, fold the cyber limit into the first sentence's list rather than adding a standalone sentence. The "deviation" status is correct: before the edit the clause failed the fallback outright on cyber/privacy, so a redline was warranted rather than a compliant-at-fallback note.

COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7(a) caps both parties, so mutuality is satisfied, and 7(b) excludes lost profits and indirect/consequential damages mutually. The clause nonetheless fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) the basis is total fees paid for the relevant Services rather than 12 months' fees, so on a short or front-loaded engagement Contractor's exposure can fall below six months' fees; and (ii) there is no usable carve-out — the sole exception points to "PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF", which in this document is the Independent Contractor clause and not an indemnity, so indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct all sit inside the cap. Our edit re-bases both caps to fees paid in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and adds a mutual, expressly uncapped Excluded Claims definition, while preserving the existing Paragraph 9 exception (which benefits us) verbatim. Contractor's cap remains scoped to Services under a Statement of Work while Company's covers the Agreement generally; that asymmetry favours us and is left unchanged. Preferred-only items (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs, and payment obligations outside the cap) are noted but not pressed.

verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: mutuality was already present, the basis is now expressly twelve (12) months of fees paid, and a mutual Excluded Claims definition places indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside both caps. The carve-out is operative for both sentences because the inserted lead-in states Excluded Claims "ARE UNCAPPED FOR EITHER PARTY", so the Company-cap sentence is not left contradicting the exception. Preferred remains unmet on five items the drafter must add if pressing the preferred position: (i) "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor; (ii) "paid or payable" rather than "paid"; (iii) data protection and security obligations in Excluded Claims; (iv) fraud and infringement of the other party's IP in Excluded Claims; (v) an express statement that Company's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. Minimality holds: the only deletions are the cap-basis words "FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES", which are the target of the 12-months-of-fees element; the favourable Paragraph 9 exception, the Statement-of-Work scoping of Contractor's cap and the mutual 7(b) exclusion are retained verbatim, and no survival tail, expense language or extra damages categories were added. Intent is preserved: the pre-existing (and pre-existing ambiguous) "PARAGRAPH 9" cross-reference is untouched rather than newly created, no defined term is left dangling, and the asymmetry favouring Company (Contractor's cap scoped to SOW Services) survives.
